text:
Marathon Petroleum dropped 3.5% today, extending a two-week slide of nearly 15%. The proximate driver appears to be escalating geopolitical tension in the Middle East—Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure, Iranian tanker incidents in the Strait of Hormuz, and ongoing Russia-Ukraine refinery strikes—which typically create shipping disruptions and price volatility. These events, combined with crude oil prices falling from the $95+ range two weeks ago to $89.53 today, squeeze refining margins (the profit refiners make by turning crude into gasoline and diesel).

Refinery utilization remains robust at 95.7%, so the problem isn't lack of demand or idle capacity; it's that crude is cheaper but product prices haven't fallen as much, compressing what refiners can earn per barrel processed. The two-week sell-off reflects investor concerns that geopolitical risk and lower oil prices are eroding the near-term profit outlook for the sector.
